title: Longest Palindromic Substring
interviewTips: Clarify: input constraints (n <= 1000?), any single valid answer acceptable when multiple longest palindromes exist, and character set (lowercase vs all ASCII)?
Trade-off: Expand Around Center O(n^2)/O(1) is expected interview optimal; DP O(n^2)/O(n^2) shows DP skill but wastes space; Manacher O(n)/O(n) is bonus only - mention but don't code unless asked.
Edge-case tip: handle even vs odd length centers separately, empty/single-char string, all same chars e.g. 'aaaa', and no palindrome longer than 1 e.g. 'abc'.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Brute Force Check All Substrings
approaches.intuition: Every answer is some s[i:j+1]. Enumerate all O(n^2) substrings and keep the longest one that reads the same forward and backward.
approaches.theory: There are n*(n+1)/2 substrings. Palindrome check for substring of length k costs O(k). Total O(n^3) time. Only O(1) extra space if checking in-place with two pointers, O(n) if slicing. Correct because we exhaustively examine the entire solution space.

timeComplexity.explanation: O(n^2) substrings, each palindrome check up to O(n). n=1000 is too slow.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only indices and best substring pointers, excluding output. O(n) if counting slicing/copy.

steps: best='b', check i=0: 'b' ok, 'ba' no, 'bab' yes -> best='bab', 'baba' no, 'babad' no
check i=1: 'a' , 'ab' no, 'aba' yes len 3 tie, keep 'bab', 'abad' no
check i=2+: no longer palindrome found, return 'bab' (also 'aba' accepted)

edgeCases: All same e.g. 'aaaa': returns whole string

approaches.name: Approach 2: Dynamic Programming by Interval Length
approaches.intuition: A substring s[i..j] is palindrome if ends match and inner substring is palindrome. Build up from short to long intervals and remember results.
approaches.theory: Define dp[i][j]=true if s[i..j] palindrome. Base: dp[i][i]=true, dp[i][i+1]=(s[i]==s[i+1]). Transition for len>=3: dp[i][j]=(s[i]==s[j] && dp[i+1][j-1]). Fill by increasing length so dp[i+1][j-1] already computed. Track max length start. Time O(n^2), space O(n^2).

timeComplexity.explanation: Fill n^2 DP table, each cell O(1) transition.

spaceComplexity.explanation: n x n boolean table. Can be optimized to O(n) with rolling array but loses start tracking simplicity.

steps: init diag true, check len2: dp[1][2]=true since 'b'=='b', start=1 maxLen=2

edgeCases: Even palindrome only e.g. 'cbbd' needs len2 base case
Odd palindrome e.g. 'aba' uses dp[i+1][j-1] diagonal

approaches.name: Approach 3: Expand Around Center
approaches.intuition: Every palindrome has a center. Try each of 2n-1 centers (n odd + n-1 even) and expand outward while characters match, keeping the longest expansion.
approaches.theory: Mirror property: if s[l..r] palindrome, s[l-1..r+1] palindrome iff s[l-1]==s[r+1]. Expanding from center enumerates all palindromes with that center in linear time. Over all centers O(n^2) time, O(1) space. This is interview-optimal due to simplicity and constant space.

timeComplexity.explanation: 2n-1 centers, each expansion up to O(n) in worst case e.g. all 'a'.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only start, maxLen and two pointers.

steps: i=1 odd expand(1,1): 'a' -> 'bab' match -> 'ababa' fail, maxLen=3 start=0
i=2 odd expand(2,2): 'b' -> 'aba' match len3 tie, keep start=0
remaining centers no improvement, return s[0:3]='bab'

edgeCases: Even length 'bb' only found by expand(i,i+1)
Entire string palindrome e.g. 'racecar' expands to bounds

approaches.name: Approach 4: Manacher's Algorithm Linear Time
approaches.intuition: Transform string to unify odd/even, then reuse mirror radius to skip redundant expansions. Each position's palindrome radius computed in amortized O(1).
approaches.theory: Transformed T='^#a#b#...#$' makes every palindrome odd-length. Maintain center C and right boundary R of furthest palindrome. For i<R, mirror m=2*C-i gives p[i]>=min(R-i,p[m]) by symmetry; then expand only beyond R. R only moves forward O(n), so total O(n). Map back: start=(center-maxLen)/2 in original string.

timeComplexity.explanation: Each expansion advances R; R moves at most 2n steps, amortized O(1) per center.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Transformed string length 2n+3 and radius array p of same size.

steps: max p=3 at center of 'bab' (or 'aba'), start=(center-3)/2=0, return 'bab'

edgeCases: Long uniform 'a'*1000: R extends once, rest O(1) via mirror
